correctness.rationale: For all integer n>=3, represent the matching by uniform repeated-label endpoint words. The restriction of a uniform word to any chosen labels is uniform, and disjoint restrictions are independent. Exhaustive integer counts of all (2r)!/2^r relative words with 2<=r<=5 prove every distinct local joint probability used. The edge/triangle overlap counts give the stated exact variances and mixed covariance for every n, not merely enumerated sample sizes; asymptotic leading coefficients yield correlation squared 20/21. The standalone exact checker reproduces finite coefficients and global n=3..7 as a separate consistency test.

originality.rationale: The distinctive claim is the unrestricted random-chord-graph triangle variance together with its mixed covariance against the edge crossing count and nontrivial 20/21 limiting explained variance. Primary full-text comparisons reveal marginal crossings, sparse fixed-crossing enumerators, degrees and isolated chord statistics, but not this mixed triangle second-moment law. More general pattern-count moment literature could imply it, so absolute historical priority is not certified.

value.rationale: The number of edges (2-crossings) and triangles (3-crossings) are fundamental, graph-invariant local-density and clustering statistics of a random circle graph. Their complete all-n moment matrix yields a nontrivial sharp asymptotic regression statement: unlike independent-edge dense random graphs, the squared correlation tends to strictly less than one (20/21), with a 1/21 triangle-variance residual under optimal affine prediction. This is a motivated structural relationship, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a restatement of old crossing variance.
